libre.banner: **MHD-INT free edition** (open source, AGPL-3.0): the same physics engine, with 47 planets. The STANDARD and PRO editions, with 300 planets, labs and exports, are available at [solariscore.com.co](https://solariscore.com.co).
libre.termico.ayuda: Energy balance of the core (Q_CMB, mantle). Off = empirical switch (v4.1). EXPERIMENTAL (Oct 2026 audit): the current thermal balance overestimates the dynamo in stagnant-lid planets (e.g. Mars ends up with a field). Use for exploration only; validated results use the default model.
libre.atm.ayuda: Simulates photo-evaporation of the atmosphere (Owen & Jackson 2012). If it is lost, the MHI will be 0.
libre.atm.dt: ⚠️ With the atmosphere on, dt ≤ 1000 years is recommended to avoid numerical instability.
libre.atm.error: ⚠️ The planet has lost its atmosphere through photo-evaporation. MHI = 0.
libre.hist.caption: Saves this simulation to your personal history. Useful for comparing settings and keeping track.
libre.video.caption: JSON with the full time series, designed to be consumed from Manim, Blender, Sora or other video generation tools.
libre.video.puntos: {p} of {o} points (downsampled to a maximum of {m}).
libre.sint.caption: Starts from Earth as the base; the parameters not listed below (core diffusivity, stellar wind profile) keep the Earth value.
libre.sint.eps.ayuda: Tilt of the rotation axis. 23.44° for Earth, 98° for Uranus. Since you choose it yourself, it counts as 'known' data for the MHI penalty.
libre.sint.luna: The synthetic Earth has no Moon of its own (LUNAS only has the real Earth); this toggle has no effect unless you add a moon in database.py.
libre.mapa.caption: The rest of the base planet's parameters (mass, radius, star) stay fixed as in the database.
libre.mapa.aviso: ⚠️ This will run {n} simulations. High resolutions can take several minutes.
libre.mapa.fallidas: {f} of {n} combinations could not be simulated (they were left as NaN in the map, not hidden).
libre.sens.fallidas: {n} of {m} runs did not give a valid result (see the 'error' column).
